description_full: Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc. provides marine transportation services to exploration and production, oilfield service, offshore construction, and military customers in the United States and internationally. The company operates offshore supply vessels, multi-purpose support vessels, and a shore-based facility to provide logistics support and specialty services to the offshore oil and gas exploration and production industry. It also provides vessel management services, marine transportation, logistics support, subsea construction, inspection, repair and maintenance, trenching and burial services, subsea well intervention services, defense support services, and integrated marine solutions for the oilfield, renewables, defense, aerospace, telecommunications, and disaster response markets. The company was formerly known as Hornbeck-Leevac Marine Services, Inc. and changed its name to Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc. in May 2002. Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is based in Covington, Louisiana.

financial_summary: Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.3B market cap on $1.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 2% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 12% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $120M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.44× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.2% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
